Perfunctory

per-FUNK-tuh-ree · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Perfunctory is casually and hastily completed, without real care.

The manager's perfunctory 'great job, everyone' at the end of the shift felt more like a formality than real praise.

Worked Example

The building inspector walked through the apartment in under two minutes, gave a perfunctory nod, and signed off without checking a single outlet.

Going through the motions quickly, without any real attention or care, is exactly the hollow, dutiful minimalism perfunctory describes.

How Strong Is It? — cursory → halfhearted → perfunctory

cursory vs. perfunctory

cursory vs. perfunctory: He gave the report a cursory read before signing off, catching only the biggest errors.

halfhearted vs. perfunctory

halfhearted vs. perfunctory: The team's halfhearted effort in the second half cost them the game entirely.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — per-

prefix — per-: through, thoroughly (Latin)

root — -funct- (fungi)

root — -funct- (fungi): to perform, discharge (Latin)

suffix — -ory

suffix — -ory: characterized by (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Perfunctory comes from Latin per- ('through') plus fungi ('to perform, discharge a duty') and -ory ('characterized by') -- perfunctus meant simply 'gotten through.' Something perfunctory is done just to get it over with, without real care or interest.

Use the root in a new word: function

Use the root in a new word: function: The function of the seatbelt warning light is simply to remind drivers to buckle up before the car will stop chiming.

Word Choice

Perfunctory criticizes the lack of genuine care or interest behind an action, even when the action itself gets technically completed -- contrast it with vapid, which describes something empty of substance rather than done half-heartedly.
